mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine typically costs £1,800-£3,000 supply-only, depending on supplier and condition. Used units start from £600. Reconditioned units range £1,100-£1,800. Supply & fit adds £400-£900 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £4,800-£6,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi (EH5) engine problems are AdBlue injector crystallisation triggering countdowns, camshaft chain wear on early 7mm-chain units (2019-2022), injector seal wear causing oil dilution, and DPF blockage from short-journey driving. Stellantis has launched a customer satisfaction campaign covering camshaft chain repairs at 100% cost for eligible vehicles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound. A rebuilt unit costs £1,800-£3,000 versus £8,000-£18,000 for a comparable used 3008. With dealer replacement potentially exceeding £6,500, specialist rebuilt units offer significant savings. Check eligibility for Stellantis's customer satisfaction campaign - camshaft chain repairs may be covered at 100%.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi (EH5) engine typically reaches 150,000-200,000 miles. Regular oil changes, AdBlue system maintenance and DPF-friendly driving (regular motorway runs) are essential for longevity. Early 2019-2022 models should have the camshaft chain inspected - Stellantis has identified a potential weakness in the 7mm chain design.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi and 1.6 BlueHDi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5 BlueHDi (EH5) replaced the 1.6 BlueHDi (DV5RC) in the second-generation 3008 from 2019. The 1.5L unit offers improved efficiency and lower emissions with a 1,499cc displacement versus the 1.6L's 1,560cc. Both use common-rail injection, but the 1.5 BlueHDi features the DV5 family's refined injection system. The 1.5 BlueHDi is generally more economical but has its own failure patterns - AdBlue injector crystallisation, injector seal wear and early camshaft chain wear.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine code is EH5 (Y01). It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi (EH5) arrived in 2019 as the latest-generation diesel option for the second-generation 3008, replacing the 1.6-litre BlueHDi units with a more efficient, refined powertrain. Part of Stellantis's DV5 engine family, the 1.5 BlueHDi delivers strong torque and excellent motorway fuel economy while meeting Euro 6d emissions standards. Available exclusively in 130hp output, it powers Active, Allure and GT Line trims - but its complex AdBlue system and early-production timing chain concerns have made it a growing source of replacement enquiries.

milestones.description: **2019** - Second-generation 3008 updated with EH5 1.5L BlueHDi 130hp (96kW) engine
**2020** - EH5 carries over with minor ECU refinements
**2021** - Peugeot issues technical bulletin on AdBlue system maintenance
**2022** - Camshaft chain width updated from 7mm to 8mm to address durability concerns
**2023** - Stellantis launches customer satisfaction campaign covering camshaft chain failures for up to 10 years / 240,000 km

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every EH5 engine fitted to the Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi (EH5) is a refined, economical diesel - but its complex emissions hardware and early-production timing chain weaknesses have created distinct failure patterns. AdBlue injector crystallisation, injector seal wear and camshaft chain wear are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. Stellantis has launched a customer satisfaction campaign covering 100% of camshaft chain repair costs for certain vehicles. Every rebuilt Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: AdBlue Injector Failure - Why Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi Engines Trigger Countdowns
problems.rootCause: Crystallised urea deposits clog the AdBlue injector nozzle, triggering fault codes and eventually a countdown to engine immobilisation. The AdBlue system is sensitive to temperature variations - crystallisation is more common in cold or very hot conditions. Owners report "AdBlue system fault" warnings appearing on the dashboard.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injector, ultrasonic clean, system reset, test drive
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before countdown reaches zero

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply and fit new AdBlue injector, recalibrate system
repairOptions.longevity: Restores function; may need tank flush if contamination severe

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new emissions hardware, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if injector failure led to NOx damage or engine derate

problems.recommendation: Address AdBlue warnings immediately - a £120-£300 specialist clean can prevent a £700 injector replacement. If the countdown has started, act fast to avoid immobilisation. Replacement engines are only needed if the fault caused secondary damage. The EH5's AdBlue system is similar to the DV5RC but may have different sensor calibration - always use specialist diagnostics.
problems.cta: -> Enquire about EH5 Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine availability

problems.h4: Camshaft Chain Wear - Why Early 1.5 BlueHDi Engines Fail
problems.rootCause: Early EH5 engines used a 7mm camshaft chain that proved insufficiently durable. Chain slack can develop, leading to timing issues, engine noise and, in severe cases, chain breakage and engine failure. Stellantis upgraded to an 8mm chain from 2022 onwards. The issue is shared with the DV5RC engine family.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of camshaft chain, tensioner and guides with 8mm upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended for early 2019-2022 models; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with 8mm upgraded chain components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has already broken or caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi has a 2019-2022 build date, check the camshaft chain immediately - even without symptoms. Stellantis may cover the repair at no cost. If the chain has already broken, a rebuilt EH5 engine with the 8mm upgraded chain is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EH5 Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Seal Wear - Why Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi Engines Suffer Oil Dilution
problems.rootCause: Injector seals degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to leak past the injector and causing oil dilution. This can lead to increased oil levels, reduced lubrication and potential engine damage. The EH5's injector seal design is similar to the DV5RC but may have different wear characteristics at higher mileage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of injectors, replacement of seals, recutting of injector seats
Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new injectors and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if injector failure has caused cylinder head damage

problems.recommendation: Injector seal wear on the Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi is a known issue that should be addressed promptly. If you notice rising oil levels or a diesel smell in the oil, have the injector seals inspected. A specialist can replace seals and recut seats in around four hours. If the vehicle has a history of multiple injector failures or the head is damaged, a rebuilt engine may be more cost-effective.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EH5 Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: DPF Blockage - Why 1.5 BlueHDi Engines Trigger Anti-Pollution Faults
problems.rootCause: Short-journey driving prevents the DPF from reaching regeneration temperature, causing soot buildup that blocks exhaust flow and triggers anti-pollution warnings. The EH5's DPF is sensitive to urban driving patterns, much like the DV5RC.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic reset, extended high-speed drive or forced regen cycle
repairOptions.longevity: Works if blockage is early-stage and sensors are functional

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove DPF for off-car cleaning or supply fitted replacement unit
repairOptions.longevity: Restores function if substrate isn't melted or cracked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new DPF, EGR, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Needed if blockage caused turbo or piston damage

problems.recommendation: For a Peugeot 3008 1.5 BlueHDi used mainly for short trips, invest in regular motorway runs to allow DPF regeneration. If the anti-pollution warning appears, address it promptly before blockage becomes severe. A rebuilt engine is only necessary if the DPF has caused turbo or internal damage.
